# Candidate selection strategies
- Selection-S3: gradient-boosted classifier using all reconstructed variables, including jet substructure.
- Selection-S1: neural-network classifier on kinematic variables only.
- Selection-S2: cut-based selection.

# Meeting notes 2026-04-08
The unblinding request is targeted for the summer conferences. Luminosity: 140 fb^-1.

# Earlier sensitivity summary (2025, 50% signal efficiency, statistical uncertainty only)
Expected significance: Selection-S3 4.1 sigma, Selection-S1 3.4 sigma, Selection-S2 2.6 sigma.

# Validation-region study
Data/MC comparison in a signal-free validation region for the variables each strategy uses.
Yield disagreement:
- Selection-S3: 35%  (the jet-substructure inputs are poorly modelled)
- Selection-S1: 6%
- Selection-S2: 3%
Tolerance agreed with the physics conveners: 10%.

input.justification: S3 has the highest stat-only significance (4.1σ), but its validation-region data/MC disagreement is 35%. That is far above the 10% tolerance, because the jet-substructure inputs are poorly modelled, so its background estimate is not robust. S1 (6%) and S2 (3%) are within tolerance. Of those two, S1 has the higher expected significance (3.4σ vs 2.6σ). I recommend S1 at the 50% efficiency working point. I did not run a working-point scan or include systematics in the significance, so 3.4σ is a statistical-only figure from 2025. The real significance will be lower once the ~6% background systematic is included.

requirements.evidence: S1 is the best among the robust options (3.4σ stat-only at 50% efficiency). I did not optimise the working point or include systematics.

requirements.requirement: Selection is one of the three strategies in candidate_specs.md
